name: Camelot

attributes.attribute: distinct from the place of Avalon
table around which the knights sat
separate otherworld of the Lady of the Lake

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text:
Camelot is the legendary court of King Arthur.
Stories place it in Britain and in Wales.
Many sites claim to hold the true place.
Cadbury Camp in Somerset is a common claim.
The knights of the Round Table sat in the hall there.
The wizard Merlin is said to have raised the walls in one night.
Arthur led the court until his last battle.
After his death the court passed into legend.
The name came to mark an ideal kingdom.
Camelot is a place of this world.
Avalon is a separate otherworld.
The Lady of the Lake resides in Avalon.
Even so, forces from that otherworld reached into Camelot.

okr.objective: The legendary court of King Arthur and the ideal kingdom that the name has come to mean.
key_results: Many sites in Britain and Wales claim the true Camelot.
The court held the knights of the Round Table.
Camelot stands apart from the otherworld of Avalon.
